task_contract.anchor_definition: The anchor is the first target-specific proof-token value-construction function on the dynamic behavior chain: the earliest function, after routing, input preparation, runtime slot selection and tuple materialization, whose own body constructs the target observable account_proof value rather than merely collecting inputs, dispatching control, packaging the result, or emitting it to the sink.

runtime_boundary.event_plane: DOM CustomEvent on the main document

evidence: The DevTools-visible JavaScript corpus is a single obfuscated bundle and no source map is exposed to the agent.
The target field name is assembled from character-code arrays at the sink, so direct literal search is insufficient.
The target account proof token is carried through runtime-derived transport keys and recovered shortly before console output.
The submit route selects its live proof-token derivation configuration only after click-time DOM, form-order, style and dataset state are captured.

The click path crosses delegated event handling, action routing, gate checks, tuple construction, asynchronous scheduling, local event dispatch, runtime slot materialization, proof-token derivation, dynamic transport and sink wrapping.
The same submit interaction emits non-target prepare/audit objects carrying account_proof-like values before the target account.submit object.
The deployed bundle also contains proof-like, state-like and vendor-like decoys that execute or remain reachable-looking without feeding the target account_proof field.
The target value is separated from the click by Promise, microtask, timer, animation-frame, MutationObserver and DOM CustomEvent boundaries.
The selected runtime configuration is cloned and mutated in a WeakMap-backed materialization step before the proof constructor receives it.
The final sink receives an already encoded account proof token after dynamic cell and lane recovery, so sink inspection alone does not identify the construction site.

behavior_category.reason: The observable field is a deterministic proof token derived from submitted account fields and runtime-selected reducer context. It behaves like a client-side seal for the submission, but this case does not issue a real network request.

near_categories.why_not: The output is not a byte array; byte-payload code in the bundle is decoy material and does not feed the target account_proof field.
The output is not merely a serialized UI state snapshot; it is a mixed proof token for the account submission.
No network request body is emitted or rewritten; the target is a console-observable account proof token.
The chain uses local DOM and form state, not browser/device capability collection as the target behavior.
